samples.text:
In recent years, buying second-hand clothes has become more popular in many countries. This essay will explain the reasons for this trend and suggest some other ways that people can reduce the environmental damage caused by their clothes.

There are several reasons why people are interested in second-hand clothing. The first reason is money. Used clothes are much more cheaper than new ones, and many people, especially students, do not have a lot of money to spend. Secondly, people are more aware about environmental problems now. They know that fashion industry produces a lot of pollution and waste, so buying used items is a way to help the planet. Also, it is very easy to buy second-hand clothes today because there are many websites and apps where people can sell their old clothes. Some young people also think that vintage clothes look more unique and fashionable.

Apart from buying used clothes, there are other steps people can take. Firstly, they can buy less clothes and choose items with good quality that last for a long time. Cheap fast fashion clothes often break after few months and then they are thrown away. Secondly, people can repair their clothes instead of throwing them when there is a small hole. Thirdly, they can give their unwanted clothes to charity shops or recycle them, so they do not go to landfill. Finally, people can choose brands which use organic cotton or recycled materials.

In conclusion, second-hand clothes are popular because they are cheap, easy to buy and good for the environment. People can also help by buying fewer and better clothes, repairing them and recycling. If everyone do these things, the fashion industry will be less harmful.
samples.why: Both parts covered with relevant reasons and steps · ideas listed rather than developed · mechanical sequencing (Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly) · adequate vocabulary · errors in comparatives, articles and agreement that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Second-hand clothing, once associated mainly with people on low incomes, is now attracting a much wider range of buyers. This essay will discuss the reasons behind this change and outline further measures that consumers can take to make their clothing choices more sustainable.

One key reason for the growing popularity of used clothes is greater environmental awareness. Many consumers have learnt through the media that the fashion industry consumes enormous amounts of water and energy and generates vast quantities of textile waste. Buying pre-owned garments allows them to enjoy new outfits without adding to this demand. Financial factors also play a role, as rising living costs have encouraged people to look for affordable alternatives, and good-quality items can often be bought for a fraction of their original price. In addition, online resale platforms have made the process far more convenient. Instead of searching through crowded charity shops, shoppers can now browse thousands of items on their phone and have them delivered to their door.

There are, however, several other ways people can reduce the environmental impact of their wardrobes. The most effective is simply to buy fewer clothes and to choose durable ones. A well-made coat that lasts ten years is clearly less harmful than several cheap ones which wears out after a single season. People can also extend the life of their clothes by washing them less frequently and at lower temperatures, and by repairing minor damage rather than discarding the item. Finally, consumers can support brands that are transparent about their supply chains and use recycled or organic materials, which puts pressure on the wider industry to change its practices.

In conclusion, the rise of second-hand shopping reflects growing environmental concern, economic pressure and the convenience of online platforms. Alongside this, buying less, caring for clothes properly and choosing responsible brands can make a significant difference.
samples.why: Both questions answered with clear, supported points · logical progression with a clear topic per paragraph · good topic vocabulary (pre-owned garments, supply chains) · frequent error-free sentences with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Charity shops and online resale platforms are enjoying a surge in popularity, as buyers who would once have insisted on new clothes increasingly choose pre-owned alternatives. This shift reflects a combination of ethical, economic and cultural factors, and while it is a positive development, it is only one of several ways in which consumers can make their clothing habits more sustainable.

Perhaps the most significant driver is a heightened awareness of the environmental cost of fashion. Widespread media coverage has exposed the industry's heavy use of water, its reliance on synthetic fibres and the mountains of discarded garments that end up in landfill, prompting many shoppers to reconsider their habits. Economic pressures reinforce this trend: with household budgets under strain, a designer jacket at a fraction of its retail price is an attractive proposition. Cultural attitudes have also shifted. Among younger consumers in particular, vintage clothing is seen not as a sign of hardship but as a way of expressing individuality, and resale apps have made browsing for such items as effortless as shopping on the high street.

Beyond buying second-hand, the single most effective step is to consume less. Choosing fewer, better-made garments and wearing them for longer reduces demand for new production far more than any recycling scheme. Caring for clothes properly also matters; washing at lower temperatures, air-drying rather than tumble-drying, and carrying out simple repairs can extend a garment's life considerably. When items are no longer wanted, they should be donated, swapped or sold rather than thrown away. Finally, consumers can use their purchasing power to reward manufacturers that are transparent about their supply chains and that use recycled or responsibly sourced materials.

In conclusion, the appeal of second-hand clothing stems from environmental concern, financial prudence and changing tastes. Its benefits can be multiplied if people also buy less, look after what they own and support genuinely responsible brands.
samples.why: Fully addresses both parts with well-developed, prioritised ideas · skilful paragraphing and cohesion · wide, idiomatic vocabulary (surge, proposition, purchasing power) · a wide range of structures with no noticeable errors.
